Definition: of Latin origin; a rheda, i.e. four-wheeled carriage (wagon for riding):--chariot.
BiblicalUsage: This word never occurs in the Greek New Testament. It is a Latin loanword for a four-wheeled carriage, listed in the lexicon but with no verse behind it, and every chariot in the King James New Testament translates a different Greek word.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that an honest word study says so plainly when a word has no verse, rather than inventing one for it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
